title: FedEx Launches Guangzhou Baiyun Airport International Cargo Terminal 4 to Accelerate GBA Trade and Global Connectivity
summary: New facility combines AI, automation, and smart customs clearance capabilities to strengthen cross-border trade, e-commerce, manufacturing, and healthcare supply chains across South China and the Greater Bay Area
body_markdown:
**Guangzhou, China, November 16, 2026** — Federal Express Corporation (FedEx), one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, today announced the official launch of FedEx Guangzhou Baiyun Airport International Cargo Terminal 4 (the “International Cargo Terminal”), a major investment that strengthens logistics connectivity between South China, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (the Greater Bay Area), and global markets. This move also further strengthens the company’s logistics network and service capabilities in China, supporting cross-border trade, e-commerce growth, advanced manufacturing, and healthcare supply chains, while helping small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) access global market opportunities.


The FedEx International Cargo Terminal is an important outcome of the collaboration between FedEx and Guangdong Airport Authority to advance the development of Guangzhou International Air Cargo Hub. Operating in close coordination with the FedEx Asia Pacific Hub, the International Cargo Terminal marks an important milestone in the company’s ongoing efforts to enhance the global connectivity of Chinese businesses. It underscores the evolution of FedEx in Guangzhou from having established a presence in the city to deepening its long-term commitment in the Greater Bay Area, further enhancing Guangzhou’s role as a critical node in global supply chains and the city’s capacity to attract, consolidate, and distribute global trade flows.


The facility integrates warehousing, sorting, and customs supervision within approximately 45,000 square meters of operational space. Currently employing about 600 team members, the facility is designed to handle both small parcels and heavyweight freight shipments. Its intelligent sorting system can process up to 28,000 shipments per hour at peak capacity, more than tripling previous processing capability, while annual cargo handling capacity exceeds 100,000 metric tons. By significantly expanding throughput and operational efficiency, the facility will help businesses move goods faster, improve supply chain resilience and respond more effectively to evolving global trade demands.


The International Cargo Terminal also showcases the company’s continued investment in digital innovation and intelligent logistics. Leveraging advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence, automation and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technologies, the Cargo Terminal enhances shipment visibility, maintains operational accuracy at more than 99%. Developed in collaboration with customs authorities, its smart customs-supervised warehouse incorporates digital capabilities including electronic documentation, pre-declaration, and intelligent alerts, to help streamline customs clearance. The facility also provides 24/7 smart supervision to meet the needs of night flights and time-critical shipments.


Additionally, the facility incorporates energy-efficient features including natural daylighting, smart lighting systems, and green landscaping. Electric forklifts, charging infrastructure, and intelligent energy management systems further support the company’s efforts to reduce its environmental impact while maintaining operational excellence.


“China remains a strategic priority in the global growth strategy of FedEx. The launch of the FedEx Guangzhou Baiyun Airport International Cargo Terminal reflects our continued commitment to strengthening our presence and investment in the Chinese market,” said Poh-Yian Koh, President of FedEx China. “As global trade continues to evolve, businesses are placing greater demands on supply chains to be more efficient, reliable, and resilient. By combining our extensive global network, with digital and intelligent logistics, we are helping Chinese businesses achieve growth through more agile, smarter, and more reliable logistics solutions.”


From signing of the agreement with Guangdong Airport Authority for the lease and operation of the FedEx Asia Pacific Hub in 2005, to its official launch at Guangzhou Baiyun Airport in 2009 — the first regional hub established in China by an international express company — and now to the opening of this facility, the company’s collaboration with Guangzhou has evolved from “planting roots” to becoming “deep-rooted” in the Greater Bay Area. Working alongside the FedEx Asia Pacific Hub, the International Cargo Terminal will further strengthen trade connectivity between the Greater Bay Area, the Asia-Pacific region, and major markets across Europe, the Americas, and the Middle East.


The Greater Bay Area is one of China’s most opened-up and economically dynamic regions in the country, with a total economic output exceeding RMB 15 trillion in 2025\[1\]. The region continues to demonstrate strong resilience and momentum in foreign trade. In the first three quarters of this year, the nine mainland cities in the Greater Bay Area recorded total imports and exports of RMB 8.42 trillion, up 24.7% year on year and accounting for 21.1% of China’s total imports and exports\[2\].


Following the launch of the facility, businesses across South China will gain faster and more efficient access to global customers and suppliers and growth opportunities through the FedEx network, which serves more than 220 countries and territories worldwide. In addition, the volume of shipments handled by FedEx through Guangzhou is expected to grow. This will further strengthen Guangzhou’s ability to serve as a all-round gateway composite international aviation hub, while enhancing the Greater Bay Area’s air logistics connectivity with global markets, improving cargo turnover efficiency, and reducing overall logistics costs.
